label: Rubin/DP2/object_collection
name: Rubin Data Preview 2 (DP2) Object
description: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) is a 10-year astronomical survey designed to map the entire southern sky in unprecedented detail. It aims to address key questions about dark energy, dark matter, the structure of the Milky Way, and the solar system. This catalog collection was generated by the DASH pipeline and it contains information about astronomical objects. Learn how to access the data through the link below.

notes.title: Additional columns
notes.content:
This catalog includes several columns added on top of the original Rubin data products:

  • Magnitude and magnitude error columns converted from fluxes: {band}_psfMag, {band}_kronMag, and {band}_cModelMag for the u, g, r, i, z, y bands (object table), and nested column objectForcedSource.psfMag, each with a corresponding error column. The magnitude error is defined as half the difference between the magnitudes corresponding to Flux ± FluxErr.
  • Four new nested columns: objectForcedSource.psfFluxErr_corrected, objectForcedSource.psfDiffFluxErr_corrected, objectForcedSource.psfFluxErr_corrected_flag, and objectForcedSource.psfDiffFluxErr_corrected_flag, produced by a model trained to correct flux errors for non-variable objects so their reduced χ² is close to unity. These corrected values may be useful for light-curve fitting; the flag is set when the ratio between the original and corrected error is outside the [0.1, 50] interval (details in Malanchev et al., in prep.; source code on GitHub).
  • Nested column objectForcedSource.psfMagErr_corrected, derived from psfFluxErr_corrected the same way the other magnitude errors are derived from flux errors.
  • Nested column objectForcedSource.midpointMjdTai, joined from the visit table for the corresponding visit.

Some float64 columns were downcast to float32 to reduce catalog size. The {band}_ra and {band}_dec columns were downcast, which may cause precision loss when the float32 rounding error exceeds the corresponding {band}_raErr/{band}_decErr. Downcast columns: exponential_dec, exponential_ra, g_dec, g_epoch, g_ra, i_dec, i_epoch, i_ra, r_dec, r_epoch, r_ra, sersic_dec, sersic_ra, u_dec, u_epoch, u_ra, y_dec, y_epoch, y_ra, z_dec, z_epoch, z_ra.
